medium_value.description: Resolve the scope contradiction by explicitly allowing the opt-in migration of the simple-release guard while excluding classifier changes and other release-guard changes. Update D-1 to match FR-1.

Define whether failed-content-read warnings include the new base .reviewignore lookup, whether a confirmed absence warrants a warning, and whether warnings are deduplicated across retries. Require filenames and provider outcomes to be rendered as single-line, control-character-safe text.

Define separate validation gates for the PR head and the resulting main merge commit, and enumerate which required checks must complete successfully. State how skipped, cancelled, neutral, superseded, and failed optional runs affect eligibility.

Require an end-to-end entry point for the opt-in fix through the supported mount or update command, including flag propagation, help text, and an integration test. Include the necessary entry-point files in the authorized write scope.

Define one supported YAML expression subset for both yq and fallback detection. Require job-scoped matching and tests for other jobs with identical guards, comments, expression wrappers, multiline values, and duplicate or ambiguous keys; refuse an opt-in rewrite when the target cannot be identified uniquely.

Specify how an explicit fix refusal propagates to the invoking command. Require a distinguishable unsuccessful outcome for a customized or ambiguous guard, while preserving exit 0 for ordinary warning-only remounts.

Define typed local-read outcomes that distinguish a missing base commit, a missing file at an available commit, and other Git failures. Trigger the contents fallback only for the specified eligible outcome and add tests for each case.

Define the base-pattern override as an explicit resolution result that distinguishes unresolved, resolved with patterns, and resolved absent. Test an empty base file and an API 404 while the checkout contains conflicting patterns.

Specify that the contents request targets the PR base repository and pinned base SHA, including fork PRs. Add a fixture with different head and base repository identities and assert the request arguments.

Define the one-call budget across paged-fetch retries and repeated selection passes. Cache successful and absent resolutions by base repository and SHA, and add a retry-path test that verifies the promised call limit.

Extend the FR-2 acceptance matrix to cover a provider without getFileContent, local mode, authentication failure, and content exactly at and above the byte limit. Require API content to pass the same parsing and validation rules as local base content.

Replace the subjective 'if cheap' condition for FR-3(e) with an explicit implementation or deferral decision. If implemented, require trusted configuration to be resolved before invalid head values are ignored, preserve failure on invalid or unavailable trusted configuration, and test all three named fields in both modes. If deferred, create a linked follow-up before closing bd-gyrgq.

Enumerate the local-read failure classes that trigger the contents-API fallback. Specify that only 'base commit not present in the clone' triggers it, determined by an explicit object-existence check (e.g. `git cat-file -e <base_sha>^{commit}`) rather than by parsing `git show` stderr, and that local oversize/binary/git-unavailable failures keep today's `base_unavailable` path without an API call.

Add an AC to FR-3 (d): a repository-wide search for the literal `[pattern:` returns no hits outside CHANGELOG and tests (covering shell scripts, docs, and any coverage consumers), and the change is listed under a 'Removed' heading in CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`. Name both `excluded[]` and `omitted[]` arrays in the criterion.

Pin the `yq` flavour and syntax the scaffold accepts (mikefarah v4 vs python-yq produce different CLI behaviour), add a risk row for divergence between the `yq` and `grep` branches, and require both detection branches to run in CI (install or stub `yq` in the bats job) rather than only testing the fallback.

Define detection as a match on the distinctive legacy fragment `pr_type != 'cycle'` on any `if:` line (warn), while the rewrite requires whitespace-normalised equality with the full legacy text (fix). State explicitly how the `grep` fallback scopes to the `simple-release` job, or that it does not need to because the fragment is unique.

Add an observability requirement: when the API fallback supplies the base `.reviewignore`, emit one stderr notice line (not a degrade) stating the base commit was not in the clone and the file was read via the contents API, so operators can distinguish the two `base` paths.
Name the 'four pipeline / scaffold bats files' in the KPIs (only two are cited elsewhere), and replace `sprint-<global>` with `sprint-280` in Success Criteria.

Add to FR-4 Acceptance Criteria the gates listed elsewhere as constraints: CI mirror run from the landed head, secret scan before each push, `tools/check-prompt-budget.sh` green if SKILL.md changed, and `checksums.json` / REPO-MAP / dist manifest regenerated in the same commit.

Add a documentation AC to FR-2: update any operator guidance (SKILL.md, `resources/exclusions-and-coverage.md`, CHANGELOG notes from cycle-135) that currently tells shallow-checkout users to fetch the base ref, so it reflects the new fallback and the cases where deepening is still needed.

State a rollback path for FR-2 and FR-3 (d): because no release ships this cycle, a single-commit revert before the next tag is the rollback, and the record/archive steps must not be blocked by it. Optionally add a configuration or environment switch to disable the contents-API fallback.

Add to FR-3 (e) an explicit fail-closed clause and test: in pull-request mode, when the head `protected_paths` / `exclude_patterns` / `max_content_fetches` is invalid AND the trusted base config is unavailable or itself invalid, the run must still fail with a config error. Only downgrade to WARN when a valid trusted value exists to govern.

Refine the 404 → `none` rule in FR-2: classify as `none` only when the provider response indicates the path is absent at a known commit; treat 'No commit found for the ref' / repo-not-found / permission-shaped 404s as `base_unavailable`. Add a test case for an unknown-ref 404.

Require the opt-in fix to verify the single-line form of the `if:` value before rewriting, independent of whether detection came from `yq` or `grep`, and to refuse otherwise. Add acceptance criteria that the rewritten workflow still parses as YAML (and passes `actionlint` when available) and preserves the original indentation and `${{ }}`/quoting wrapper.

Specify how the opt-in flag reaches `scaffold_post_merge_workflow` (positional argument vs environment variable such as `LOA_FIX_RELEASE_GUARD=1`), which entry points invoke the detection (`/mount` only, or also `/update-loa`), and the exit code on refusal. Add an AC that the WARN is emitted from each entry point that re-runs the scaffold.

Define bd-nr5i6 in the PRD (one line: what it is and why the WARN cites it) and require the WARN to carry an operator-actionable remedy: the exact replacement line and the fix flag name, with the bead id as a secondary reference or dropped from the user-facing text.

State whether the base `.reviewignore` contents read counts against `max_content_fetches` (recommended: it does not, it is a control-plane read) and add a test that a run with `max_content_fetches: 0` still performs the `.reviewignore` read.

Add acceptance criteria for the stated assumptions: (1) a fixture adapter without `getFileContent` → today's `base_unavailable` + degrade, no throw; (2) local mode (no PR) → no API call; (3) the resolved base patterns are memoised so repeated `attempt` invocations (page retries, budget retries) do not re-issue the call.

For FR-3 (c), specify the emission mechanism (e.g. `process.stderr.write` with the `[bridgebuilder] WARN:` prefix) since the Problem Statement says `paged-fetch.ts` has no logger, cap or aggregate the output (one line per outcome class or a summary count) to avoid one line per file in a rate-limit cascade, and state whether this WARN also covers the FR-2 `.reviewignore` read failure.

Move FR-3 (e) (head-side scope validation) into its own requirement (FR-5, Could Have) or a new bead, and keep bd-gyrgq's close criterion at (a)–(d). Update the Executive Summary, which lists four debts, to match.

blockers.concern: PR-mode validation downgrades are not explicitly conditional on successful loading and validation of the trusted replacement configuration.
blockers.why_matters: If implemented, malformed head configuration combined with a failed trusted read could allow review to continue with defaults or partially applied head values, weakening protected paths or review limits.
blockers.recommendation: Permit a warning only after a valid trusted replacement is available. Define fail-closed behavior for trusted read or validation failures and test each affected field, including fork and environment-based PR detection.

blockers.concern: The grep/sed fallback for FR-1 has no YAML structural awareness. 'Line-anchored' grep for `if:` cannot tell the `simple-release` job's `if:` from a step-level `if:` inside that job, a second job that copied the legacy guard, or a comment. The opt-in rewrite could therefore change the wrong line in a downstream operator's CI workflow and the acceptance fixtures (one clean legacy file) would still pass.
blockers.why_matters: Rewriting the wrong `if:` silently corrupts a user-owned workflow file in a repository we do not control; the operator discovers it only when their Post-Merge Pipeline misbehaves. 'diff shows one changed line' is satisfied even when it is the wrong line.
blockers.location: FR-1 Description (yq-absent fallback) and the opt-in flag; Risks table row 1
blockers.recommendation: Scope both detection and rewrite to the `simple-release` job block (awk range from the `simple-release:` key to the next key at the same indentation), match only the job-level `if:` at the expected indentation, require exactly one match and refuse otherwise. Add bats fixtures with a step-level `if:`, a second job carrying the legacy text, and the legacy text in a comment; assert the file is unchanged in each.

blockers.concern: The scaffold fallback does not specify how it proves that a matched if: line belongs to simple-release, and the yq path may recognize multiline expressions that the one-line rewrite cannot safely replace.
blockers.why_matters: An opt-in repair could change another job's condition or leave continuation lines behind, producing an invalid workflow or changing release behavior.
blockers.recommendation: Require unambiguous identification of the simple-release job and a supported single physical if: line before rewriting. Refuse multiline, duplicate, aliased, or ambiguous forms consistently with and without yq; test neighboring jobs and multiline conditions.

blockers.concern: The shipping gate requires green checks and a non-degraded Bridgebuilder verdict without explicitly requiring both to apply to the final reviewed commit.
blockers.why_matters: A later fix, regenerated artifact, or PR update could invalidate the recorded verdict while the automation still merges using stale review evidence.
blockers.recommendation: Bind required checks and the Bridgebuilder verdict to the exact final PR head SHA, invalidate approval after any head change, and define how required skipped or neutral checks are handled.
